segments.text: My family is raising eight-year-old twin daughters, Emma and Sophia.
Their resemblance is striking, but their personalities are characteristically different.
Emma is logical and thinks about things in an orderly way
She is good at math and science
And she often devises puzzles to entertain the family
Sophia, on the other hand, is sensitive and artistic
She draws, sings, and reads out the story she has made up to the family
Even adults can be astonished at her power of expression
Genetically identical twins share nearly the same genes
Yet as they grew, each one's personality has become more and more distinct
This provides an interesting reference
For studies of nature versus nurture
Genes alone do not determine personality
Environment, experience, and the person's own choices
Shape each one, if even twins differ
Of course, every human is unique
What matters in raising a child is respecting each one's personality
Making Emma draw the same picture as Sophia is pointless
Making Sophia solve the same puzzle as Emma is painful
The parent's role is to cultivate each child's strengths
But parents are not the only ones who raise excellent human beings
School teachers, friends, local community
And the child's own effort
All together they shape a single person
Emma and Sophia are growing up today
Quarrelling and laughing as they grow up
What kind of adults will they become?
As a parent, I am eagerly looking forward to it
